rendered:
According to the document, the review uses the total global cobalt reserves obtained from the United States Geological Survey 2021 report on cobalt (7 million metric tons) and assumes a conservative ≈70% yearly mining efficiency with ≈40% of the mined cobalt directed toward battery manufacturing.

To calculate the cobalt usable for batteries, the review multiplies the total global cobalt reserves by the assumed mining efficiency and the percentage directed toward battery manufacturing:

7,000,000 metric tons (total global cobalt reserves) × 0.7 (yearly mining efficiency) × 0.4 (percentage directed toward battery manufacturing) = 2,240,000 metric tons

So, the review estimates that the total usable cobalt from the total reserves for battery industries is approximately 2,240,000 metric tons.
